name: The Beast
title: The Poster Credit That Started a Secret Game
claims: The Beast is an alternate reality game developed by Microsoft to promote the 2001 film A.I. Artificial Intelligence | 1
The film was released June 29, 2001 | 1
Trailers and posters credited Jeanine Salla as the production's "sentient machine therapist" | 1
An obscure poster credit attributed to a fictional person led down a rabbit hole | 2
Players entered through one of three entry points called "rabbit holes" by the development team | 1
A phone number hidden in another trailer ultimately led to Jeanine | 1
A promotional poster sent to technology and entertainment media outlets had a code stating "Evan Chan was murdered. Jeanine is the key." | 1
The story is set in 2142, roughly forty years after the events of the film | 1
Evan Chan was said to be killed in a boating accident aboard his AI-enhanced boat Cloudmaker | 1
Dr. Jeanine Salla receives a cryptic message revealing he was murdered and leads an investigation | 1
Venus, a companion bot, was reprogrammed to kill Evan | 1
The cover-up triggered further murders of humans and artificial intelligences | 1
The Mann Act is brought before the legislature and president and put to referendum on whether AI is treated equal to human citizens | 1
The game launched March 8, 2001 | 1
Only roughly one hundred players discovered the game in the first few weeks | 1
Websites were registered to various individuals with the surname Ghaepetto, a reference to Geppetto, under fake phone numbers and addresses | 1
The registrations were meant to prevent a connection between the websites and the film's promotion | 1
Microsoft initially denied involvement, believed to be part of maintaining the intrigue | 1
In April, the founder of Ain't It Cool News received an email from "claviusbase," a reference to 2001: A Space Odyssey, urging him to search for Jeanine Salla | 1
He found numerous websites registered to the same IP address, including one for Bangalore World University, founded in 2028, claiming to be Jeanine's employer | 1
He posted the article on April 11, drawing 25 million hits to The Beast websites that day | 1
Over 22,000 messages about The Beast went to Ain't It Cool News over two months | 1
CNN stated the article was believed to be the first written about the game | 1
Cloudmakers is a Yahoo! Group named after the boat on which Evan was murdered | 1
Before the film's release 4,500 to nearly 5,000 users were registered to the Cloudmakers message board | 1
One player recalled about 6,000 people on the mailing list | 2
The total number of players was uncertain, but Cloudmakers was said to include a majority of them | 1
The founder said in June 2001 that the list generated tens of thousands of messages weekly | 1
The game was being developed as it was played; Cloudmakers pushed the developers and influenced the plot | 1
Messages from Cloudmakers members to characters regularly turned up in the plot; their designs, blueprints and databases were referenced by in-game websites and magazines | 1
SphereWatch, a smaller group, also had its efforts featured | 1
Clues were in trailers, print ads, posters, telephone messages, live promotional events, and restroom graffiti in major US cities | 1
Online the game used text, photograph, video and audio | 1
A player described an experience overlapping real and virtual worlds, with multiple mysteries and dozens of subplots linked by fake websites, text messages, pictures and videos | 2
In May, at an MIT presentation, producer Kathleen Kennedy and actor Haley Joel Osment accepted a question from a presumedly planted audience member about working with Jeanine Salla | 1
Kennedy afterward distributed business cards for Jeanine containing another clue | 1
Later in May, "Anti-Robot Militia" rallies in New York City, Chicago and Los Angeles were staged with actors pretending to protest AI | 1
One count says over forty websites; another says fifty with about one thousand pages | 1
A puzzle near the end required understanding lute tablature, which Cloudmakers solved | 1
The Puppetmasters admitted they relied on the knowledge of Cloudmakers and other player groups | 1
The game's creators became known as the "Puppetmasters" | 1
Jordan Weisman created the original concept; Elan Lee developed it; Sean Stewart was head writer; Pete Fenlon was producer, content lead and fourth Puppetmaster | 1
A larger creative team worked under the Puppetmasters | 1
Weisman, Lee, Stewart and others later founded 42 Entertainment, specializing in alternate reality games | 1
Jeanine Salla and other characters are listed in the film's closing credits | 1
The four original Puppetmasters were revealed and credited in the closing credits, where they placed game clues and references | 1

The game does not directly reference the film; Kennedy said its intention was to develop the film's fictional setting and lay a foundation for video games over five years in a long term project with Microsoft and Xbox | 1
The game was scheduled to end June 29, 2001, but continued through the summer | 1
The Los Angeles Times called it "one of the most elaborate movie promotions ever conceived," "unprecedented even by Hollywood standards" | 1
The Atlantic cites it as the "first truly successful alternate reality game"; Polygon stated it was the first of its kind | 1
The game failed to draw an audience to the film, which domestically grossed less than its budget | 1
Knowles believed the game's popularity pressured Spielberg and the studio, and secrecy raised expectations | 1
The game was compared to The Blair Witch Project's marketing; Knowles felt Blair Witch was more successful due to broader appeal and longer lifespan of footage | 1
One player said the community's members went on to become game designers and the game was influential for almost a generation | 2
In March 2022 The Beast received a Legacy Peabody Award in the Digital and Interactive category | 1
